section: Role of the press and newspapers in the Andhra Movement - Krishna Patrika, Andhra Patrika, Andhra Prabha, Zamin Ryot

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding newspapers associated with movements in Andhra:

List-I (Movement)

a. Vandemataram/Swadeshi movement
b. Peasant or anti-zamindari movement
c. Socialist movement
d. Communist movement

List-II (Newspaper)

i. Zamin Ryot
ii. Prajasakthi
iii. Navasakthi
iv. Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari and Navayuga

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
accepted.x: The Vandemataram/Swadeshi movement was supported by Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari and Navayuga. Zamin Ryot supported the peasant or anti-zamindari movement, Navasakthi was associated with socialism, and Prajasakthi with communism.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched movement–newspaper associations.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Navasakthi was the first fully socialist Telugu journal.
2. Prajasakthi was the first communist Telugu journal.
3. Zamin Ryot was the first fully socialist Telugu journal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: Zamin Ryot was associated with the peasant or anti-zamindari movement, while Navasakthi held the distinction of being the first fully socialist Telugu journal.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly transferred description before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.s:
Match the following women-oriented publications with the years associated with them:

a. Hindu Sundari
a. 1902
b. Sri Savitri
b. 1904

Which of the following is correct?
accepted.x: Hindu Sundari was associated with the year 1902, while Sri Savitri was associated with 1904.
accepted.tq: Match each publication with its specific year before checking the combined option.

accepted.s: Jaya Bharat holds which distinction in the history of Telugu journalism?
o: It was the first fully socialist Telugu journal.
It was the first Telugu journal published after independence.
It was the only Telugu daily of British Andhra.
It was the first Telugu newspaper published in Bellary in 1835.
accepted.x: Jaya Bharat was the first Telugu journal published after independence. Satyadoota, Navasakthi and Desabhimani respectively represent the other distinctions listed in the alternatives.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among publications by their precise historical distinction rather than by their broad association with Telugu journalism.

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes the wider significance of the press in the Andhra region during the freedom movement?
o: It opposed both the national movement and the demand for a separate Andhra.
It confined its activities exclusively to literary publishing and avoided political issues.
It spread the national movement and built support for the demand for a separate Andhra.
It functioned only as an instrument of the colonial administration.
accepted.x: The press performed a dual role: it spread the national movement and also built support for the separate-Andhra demand.
accepted.tq: Identify the option that combines both stated functions instead of accepting an extreme exclusive claim.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the social impact of newspapers in the Andhra region:
1. Newspapers gave rise to reading rooms.
2. Newspapers contributed to the development of libraries.
3. Newspapers had no role beyond reporting political events.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: newspapers gave rise to reading rooms and libraries. Statement 3 is false because their influence extended beyond merely reporting political events.
accepted.tq: Reject the restrictive statement and select the combination containing the two wider social effects.

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly identifies the first Telugu newspaper, its year of publication and its place of publication?
accepted.x: Satyadoota was the first Telugu newspaper; it was published in 1835 at Bellary.
accepted.tq: Verify all three elements—publication, year and place—rather than relying on a single familiar association.
